title: Great Minds and Masterpieces
intro: Paintings, symphonies, novels, buildings and big ideas. How well do you know the people who made them?

questions.prompt: Which Dutch artist painted 'The Night Watch'?
questions.explanation: Rembrandt finished The Night Watch in 1642. The huge group portrait hangs in the Rijksmuseum in Amsterdam.

questions.prompt: Which artist painted 'The Persistence of Memory', with its famous melting clocks?
questions.explanation: Dalí painted it in 1931. It is one of the best-known works of Surrealism, the art of dreams.

questions.prompt: Who painted 'Girl with a Pearl Earring'?
questions.explanation: Vermeer painted it in about 1665 in Delft. He is famous for his soft, glowing light.

questions.prompt: Which composer wrote 'The Four Seasons'?
questions.explanation: Vivaldi's four violin concertos, published in 1725, paint pictures of spring, summer, autumn and winter.

questions.prompt: Beethoven's Ninth Symphony ends with a choir singing which poem?
questions.explanation: Beethoven set Friedrich Schiller's 'Ode to Joy'. The melody is now the anthem of the European Union.

questions.prompt: Which child prodigy from Salzburg wrote the opera 'The Magic Flute'?
questions.explanation: Mozart was composing by the age of five. The Magic Flute was first performed in 1791, shortly before he died.

questions.prompt: Who wrote the novel 'Middlemarch'?
questions.explanation: George Eliot was the pen name of Mary Ann Evans. Middlemarch was published in parts in 1871 and 1872.

questions.prompt: Which Russian author wrote 'War and Peace'?
questions.explanation: Tolstoy's huge novel follows several families during Napoleon's invasion of Russia in 1812.

questions.prompt: Which architect designed St Paul's Cathedral in London?
questions.explanation: Wren designed the new St Paul's after the Great Fire of 1666. It was finished in 1711.

questions.prompt: Which architect designed the Sagrada Família basilica in Barcelona?
questions.explanation: Gaudí worked on the Sagrada Família from 1883 until his death in 1926. Building work has continued ever since.

questions.prompt: Which astronomer worked out the three laws of planetary motion, including that planets move in ellipses?
questions.explanation: Kepler used Tycho Brahe's careful observations to show that planets travel in ellipses, not perfect circles.

questions.prompt: Whose X-ray image, known as Photo 51, was key to discovering the double-helix structure of DNA?
questions.explanation: Rosalind Franklin's team took Photo 51 in 1952. It gave Watson and Crick vital evidence for their model.

questions.prompt: On which ship did Charles Darwin sail around the world in the 1830s?
questions.explanation: Darwin's five-year voyage on HMS Beagle, including his visit to the Galápagos Islands, shaped his ideas on evolution.

questions.prompt: Which two elements did Marie and Pierre Curie discover?
questions.explanation: The Curies discovered both in 1898. Marie named polonium after Poland, the country where she was born.

questions.prompt: Which art movement took its name from Claude Monet's painting 'Impression, Sunrise'?
questions.explanation: A critic mocked Monet's painting in 1874 by calling the group 'Impressionists'. The artists adopted the name.

questions.prompt: Which French sculptor created 'The Thinker'?
questions.explanation: The Thinker began as part of Rodin's huge doorway The Gates of Hell, inspired by Dante's poem.

questions.prompt: Michelangelo painted the ceiling of which chapel in Vatican City?
questions.explanation: Michelangelo painted the ceiling between 1508 and 1512, including the famous Creation of Adam.

questions.prompt: Which Italian poet wrote 'The Divine Comedy'?
questions.explanation: Dante's long poem, finished around 1321, follows a journey through Hell, Purgatory and Paradise.

questions.prompt: Which composer wrote the music for the ballet 'The Nutcracker'?
questions.explanation: The Nutcracker was first performed in St Petersburg in 1892. Tchaikovsky also wrote Swan Lake and The Sleeping Beauty.

questions.prompt: The painter Frida Kahlo came from which country?
questions.explanation: Frida Kahlo is known for bold self-portraits full of Mexican colour and folk art.

questions.prompt: Which ancient Greek mathematician is said to have shouted 'Eureka!' in his bath?
questions.explanation: The story goes that Archimedes realised how to measure volume when he saw his bath water rise.

questions.prompt: In which Jane Austen novel do Elizabeth Bennet and Mr Darcy appear?
questions.explanation: Pride and Prejudice was published in 1813. Austen's working title was First Impressions.

questions.prompt: Leonardo da Vinci painted 'The Last Supper' on a wall in Milan.
questions.explanation: Leonardo painted it in the 1490s on a wall of the convent of Santa Maria delle Grazie in Milan.

questions.prompt: Johann Sebastian Bach and George Frideric Handel were born in the same year.
questions.explanation: Both great Baroque composers were born in Germany in 1685, yet they never met.

questions.prompt: Albert Einstein won his Nobel Prize for the theory of relativity.
questions.explanation: Einstein's 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics was for explaining the photoelectric effect, not relativity.

questions.prompt: The Sydney Opera House was designed by a Danish architect.
questions.explanation: Jørn Utzon of Denmark won the design competition in 1957. The building opened in 1973.

questions.prompt: Charles Dickens wrote 'Wuthering Heights'.
questions.explanation: Wuthering Heights was written by Emily Brontë and published in 1847.

questions.prompt: How many symphonies did Beethoven complete?
questions.explanation: Beethoven completed nine symphonies. The Ninth, finished in 1824, was written when he was almost completely deaf.

questions.prompt: In which year did Isaac Newton publish his Principia, setting out his laws of motion and gravity?
questions.explanation: Newton's Principia, published in 1687, is one of the most important science books ever written.

questions.prompt: In which year was Charles Darwin's 'On the Origin of Species' published?
questions.explanation: On the Origin of Species came out in November 1859 and set out the theory of evolution by natural selection.
